newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - LATIN AMERICA. NORWICH UNION..
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - LATIN AMERICA. NORWICH UNION..

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN

Management consultancy Datamonitor's report on Latin America yesterday confirmed what Proteus and close observers of that region have been saying for some time: the growth prospects for insurers are immense.

Datamonitor forecasts a doubling in market size in the next five years. However, even more telling in terms of long term potential is the comparison between European and Latin American per capita spend on insurance.

For every $98 spent on average by a Brazilian on general insurance, a German spends $1,192. Brazilians spend more on general insurance than any other country in the region. In Mexico, which has attracted several foreign insurers, the average is just $25 a year.
The latest company to invest in Latin America is Spain's Mapfre, which yesterday took a majority stake in Peru's El Sol Nacional.
Peru is not included in Datamonitor's list of six powerhouse economies in the region, suggesting the Spanish insurer is taking a particularly long-term view of this market.
Australia Mutual Provident may make a bid for Britain's fifth largest insurance group Norwich Union before it floats in June, according to the latest market chatter.

AMP came out with some firm fighting talk after it lost out to Prudential in the two billion stg plus bidding war for UK life insurer Scottish Amicable. But that may be having too strong an influence on the conclusions of pundits and the trade press, which is tending to look for AMP's next possible target and make two and two equal four.
True, AMP says it is keen on a British acquisition. But they would be hard pressed to be ready to bid before the float in June. In addition, the five billion stg price tag would be difficult to meet.

There might be a chance that, if AMP could move very quickly a lower price could be struck before premium-hungry shareholders confuse the issue. But even then, policyholders would expect a windfall in place of return on the 600 shares they might get in a flotation.
